items.note: Yolk header band with a sagging arc, a 64px tight title and a person scene (crescent-shaded blue figure, orange disc cutting in, cloud, star and sparkle). There is a cream sidebar with an ink selected pill and white dot, and a crescent-initials avatar. It clearly speaks the reference's language. But the band is about 375px tall with only two lines of text at its top, so the profile form starts halfway down the first screen. The fields sit on bare white rather than in a cream group panel like 09.

Matches the phone reference (04): a compact yolk band with the title and lead on the left, the person cluster tucked about 90px into the top corner, and a shallow arc. Below it are a cream pill tab strip with category dots and the ink selected pill, chunky full-width inputs, and a cream secondary pill on its ledge. The type rhythm is as considered as the reference's.

Faithful night version: navy page, indigo sidebar, white selected pill with an ink dot, indigo inputs, and the yolk band and person scene keeping their hues, as the 03 night palette implies. It has the same tall-band problem as by day: half the first screen is yellow above a short header. The page ends in a white bottom bar.

Compact yolk band with the corner cluster on a navy page, a white selected tab pill among indigo ones, and indigo inputs with lilac borders. It reads as the same family as the reference's night band. Hierarchy is clear: title, then avatar, then fields.

Blue band with white text and a strong subject scene: a crescent-shaded yellow bell with an orange clapper, a pink disc behind it, a cloud and sparkles. The groups are cream radius-xl panels, each with a plated glyph by its title, 1px-ruled rows and trailing ink switches, which is close to the reference's cream-panel craft. The band again takes about 45% of the first screen. The off switches are a pale track on cream and nearly vanish.

Compact blue band with the bell cluster in its corner, a cream panel with a plated envelope glyph, a bold group title and ruled switch rows. Spacing is generous and even, close to the 04 phone rhythm. The off switch is faint on the cream panel, as on desktop.

Indigo group panels on navy with white 'on' tracks and an ink knob. The off tracks are indigo-on-indigo but still legible, and the blue band and bell scene carry over unchanged. It reads like the reference's night palette. The band is oversized for a settings screen, and the footer ends in a white bar.
Compact blue band, white selected tab pill, an indigo panel with a white plate behind the envelope glyph, and white/ink switches. Clear hierarchy and a calm night palette, consistent with 03.

Green band with a padlock scene (crescent-shaded orange body, ink shackle, yellow coin cutting in, cloud and sparkles). A plated key glyph opens the password group, and below it a bordered sessions table has cream row-action pills. The language is right, but the 375px band leaves a large empty green area beside a two-line header. The password fields sit on bare white instead of a cream group panel.

Compact green band with the lock cluster tucked top right, then a plated key glyph beside a bold group title and full-width inputs with a dot helper. It reads as the reference's phone layout. The selected tab is partly scrolled off the strip but still identifiable.

Navy page with indigo inputs, the green band and lock scene kept at full strength, a white plate behind the key glyph, and an indigo sessions table with red-label revoke pills. It is a credible night derivation. The band is oversized, and the page ends in a bright white footer bar.

Compact green band on navy, a white selected tab pill, a cream plate with the key glyph, and indigo inputs. The rhythm and hierarchy match the reference's phone screens, with the night palette applied consistently.

Orange band with a wallet-and-coin scene (blue wallet with a darker clasp, yellow coin rising behind it, cloud and sparkles). The plan cards are now borderless cream tiles with a spaced eyebrow and a big bold price. The current plan is the one violet field with a check disc, which closes the rc.3 bordered-plan gap and is near 08's tone-on-tone figure tiles. Below are a cream payment panel and a framed invoice table. The band is again much taller than its content needs.

Compact orange band with the wallet cluster in its corner. The plans stack as full-width cream cards with big bold prices and green ticks, and the violet current plan follows, so it is close to the reference's craft. The pill tab strip does not scroll the selected tab into view, so the current page is not shown in the strip. The plans glyph is a bar chart, a weaker subject choice than a coin.

Indigo plan cards on navy with white pills, and the violet current plan still separates from the page because it sits on the page rather than on a night band. The orange band and wallet scene keep their hues, the invoices sit in an indigo framed table, and the page ends in a white bottom bar. The band is oversized for a settings screen.

Compact orange band on navy, indigo plan cards with a white secondary pill and big bold prices, and the violet current plan below. It is consistent with the night palette. As by day, the selected tab is off-screen in the strip, so none of the visible tabs shows the current page.

findings.summary: On desktop, every settings screen opens with a header band about 375px tall (about 45% of the first screen), and it holds only a 64px title and one or two lead lines in its top-left corner. The band art has grown into a scene, which closes the rc.3 'sticker' gap, but the band now takes its height from the art instead of the text. That leaves a wide empty yolk, green or orange area below the header, and the settings content starts below mid-screen. The reference sizes a band to its content: a tall band only where it carries a hero's headline, lead, checklist and pills (02), and compact title-sized bands on phones (04). A 'compact header band' on a product screen should cost far less of the first screen than a hero.
findings.promptFix: Size a product screen's header band by its text, not its art. The band is its text block plus `space.10` above and `space.8` below, about 200–240px on desktop, never more than a third of the first screen. The art box fills the trailing 40% of the band's width and takes the band's height. Its SVG uses a wide viewBox (about 400×200) with `height: 100%; width: auto; max-width: 100%`, so the scene spreads sideways instead of growing taller. Keep the tall, art-sized band for front pages and heroes, where the band carries a headline, lead and pills.
findings.specRule: .ms-field--header { --ms-arc: var(--size-arc-sm); padding-block: var(--space-10) var(--space-8); min-height: calc(min(42vw, var(--size-band-art)) * 0.6 + var(--space-12)); } … .ms-field__art { … width: min(42%, var(--size-band-art)); }

findings.summary: In dark mode every settings page still ends in a bright white bottom bar under the indigo footer, the one light element at night. The spec maps the footer bottom bar to `surface.inverse`, which is white in the dark table. The reference's night palette (03) stays dark to the edge. This was named in rc.3 and is still open.
findings.promptFix: Give the footer bottom bar its own role token, the darkest surface in both appearances: ink by day, and at night a step darker than the navy page, with white text. Keep `surface.inverse` for small floating pieces such as toasts.
findings.specRule: Footer | Cream band with rise arc, link columns, a signup field + ink pill; `surface.inverse` bottom bar with round icon buttons … (dark) `color.surface.inverse` | `#ffffff`

findings.summary: In the light appearance, an off switch is a pale warm-grey track with a white knob on the cream group panel, so it nearly disappears. The spec's off track is `surface.hover`, one step from the cream it sits on. The reference's controls on cream (09) always separate clearly from their panel.

On phones, the horizontal pill tab strip that replaces the sidebar does not scroll the selected tab into view. On the last section's page, the ink selected pill is fully off-screen, so the strip shows no current page.
